predecessors.name: Muhammad Ali dynasty
predecessors.text: Egypt and the Sudan under the pasha, whose title became khedive by firman on 8 June 1867

successors.name: Sultanate of Egypt
successors.text: Egypt, a British protectorate under Sultan Hussein Kamel from 19 December 1914

ledger.x: 1866: the khedivial line of Muhammad Ali's Egypt begins in Cliopatria's and the preceding dossier's bookkeeping.
1866: the khedives stay Ottoman vassals.
8 June 1867: Isma'il takes the title of khedive.
1870: Egypt establishes Equatoria.
1872: Bogos and Keren are annexed.
1874: Egypt annexes Darfur.
1874: Egyptian warships patrol Tadjoura.
1875: Egypt holds the Somali coast from Zeila to Berbera.
11 October 1875: Egypt takes Harar.
October 1875: Egypt invades Hamasien.
1877: Bahr el Ghazal and the Upper Nile province appear in Cliopatria's Khedivate.
1881: the Mahdist revolution begins.
1882: Kordofan and Al Ubayyid pass to the Ansar.
September 1882: Britain defeats the Egyptian army at Tel el-Kebir and occupies Egypt.
1883: most of Darfur passes to the Ansar.
1884: the Hewett Treaty returns Bogos to Ethiopia.
1884: the war with Ethiopia ends with the Hewett Treaty ('only finishing in 1884').
1884: Egyptian rule at Harar ends.
April 1884: the Egyptians leave Tadjoura.
April 1884: the Egyptians leave the Somali coast.
1885: the rest of the Egyptian Sudan falls to the Ansar.
1885: the fighting ends with the Sudan in Mahdist hands.
1885: Equatoria is left as an isolated outpost.
February 1885: the Italians seize Massawa.
19 January 1899: Wadi Halfa passes to the condominium.
10 July 1899: Suakin goes to Sudan.
1914: the British occupation becomes a protectorate.
1914: Ottoman suzerainty over Egypt ends.
19 December 1914: the Khedivate ends and Hussein Kamel becomes sultan.

wars.name: Conquest of Darfur
wars.outcome: Egyptian conquest and annexation of Darfur in 1874.

wars.name: Capture of Harar
wars.outcome: Egyptian force from Zeila seized Harar on 11 October 1875; Egyptian governors held it to 1884.

wars.name: Ethiopian-Egyptian War
wars.outcome: Egyptian defeats at Gundet (October 1875) and Gura (March 1876); the war 'only finish[ed] in 1884' with the Hewett Treaty, when Bogos was returned to Ethiopia.

wars.name: Mahdist War
wars.outcome: The Mahdist revolution of 1881 overran the Egyptian Sudan: Kordofan fell in 1882, Darfur in 1883; Gordon held Khartoum 1884-1885 and it fell on 26 January 1885 (Mahdist State page); only Suakin and Wadi Halfa stayed in Anglo-Egyptian hands.

wars.name: Anglo-Egyptian War
wars.outcome: British victory at Tel el-Kebir in September 1882 ended the Urabi revolt and began the British occupation.

wars.name: Anglo-Egyptian conquest of the Sudan
wars.outcome: Kitchener's Anglo-Egyptian army (the Egyptian army 'mobilised and by 4 June 1896 Kitchener had assembled a force of 9,000 men') retook Dongola in September 1896 and Berber on 5 September 1898; the Khedivate page has 'Anglo-Egyptian rule was restored to the…

certainty.note: The Sudanese, Equatorial and Red Sea limits are administrative provinces with no surveyed line; the Ethiopian frontier is a battle line until the Hewett Treaty of 1884.
Egypt's desert frontiers are not described on the pages opened; the Sudan frontier and the condominium are in anglo-egyptian-sudan.
